name: Timestamp
description: Formats an ISO calendar date, instant, Unix timestamp, or Date into human-readable text: relative for recency, absolute for precision, or auto to switch between them. Date-only values retain their calendar date across runtime timezones.

ariaRequirements: Renders a semantic <time> element with a machine-readable dateTime attribute that preserves date-only versus instant precision.
Relative output carries the full date as a native tooltip (title) so the precise moment stays discoverable.
a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-07-12 (Claude): verified in Storybook 6010 — light + dark render all 8 formats readable in both tones; relative ladder correct (30s->now, minutes/hours/days/weeks/months); forced-colors safe by construction (pure <time> text, no bg/border/opacity) and confirmed via DT_FORCED_COLORS=active pass; console clean; axe green (10 tests); AT snapshots captured for all 8 stories.

value.description: The date/time to display: ISO 8601 calendar date or instant, Unix seconds, or Date.

autoThreshold.description: Seconds after which `auto` switches from relative to date_time.

tone.description: Color role: body text or muted metadata.

tooltip.description: Native tooltip with the full date when showing relative time.

live.description: Keep relative output ticking while mounted.

now.description:
Reference "now" for relative/auto output. Defaults to render time; pass a
fixed value in stories/tests for deterministic output.

locale.description: Locale override; defaults to the active site language.

forbiddenUse: wrap it in another `<time>` or add a redundant `title`; it owns both.
use `live` for values that will not change meaningfully while on screen
dense: semantic time value with locale-aware absolute, relative, and auto formats; preserves date-only values across timezones and can update live

usage.description: Timestamp renders machine-readable date and time values as localized human text. Use relative or auto formats for recent activity, absolute formats when precision matters, and system formats for technical contexts. Date-only input stays on the same calendar date regardless of the runtime timezone.

bestPractices.description: Use auto for activity metadata that should read relatively while recent and become precise as it ages.
Use date or date_time when readers must compare or cite an exact calendar value.
Pass date-only content as YYYY-MM-DD so its calendar date is preserved across runtime timezones.
Enable showTimezone for time-bearing values when the reader needs to know which timezone applies.
Do not wrap Timestamp in another time element or duplicate its machine-readable dateTime value.
Do not enable live for static historical values; periodic updates should be reserved for relative time that changes on screen.
